title: Lamps Before Dark
summary: Storm season drags the dusk in early, and Lamp Rest's rim keeps its own stubborn schedule: ninety-one lamps, eleven sulking, one proud, and tonight too few hands to walk the ring — the usual amount of too few, which is all of them. Verger Sann sends a rider out with the wick-satchel: reach each unlit arc, hold still while the wick catches, get the ring lit before the dark finishes arriving.

objectives.label: Collect the wick-satchel from Verger Sann at the temple steps
Light the west arc — hold still while each wick catches; the wind reads left to right
Light the proud lamp's arc — it expects a compliment and is not picky about the variety
Light the last lamp by the listening horn — if it hums back, hum once, politely
Return the satchel — darkness declined, with thanks

offer.text: Courier. Stock report: dusk incoming ahead of schedule, rim walk short-handed by the usual amount — which is all of it. Ninety-one lamps on that ring, eleven sulking tonight, one proud; the proud one sulks *louder* than the others if it's lit late. I need a rider with a gentle throttle and no fear of inventory.

Take the wick-satchel. Ease up to each unlit arc and hold still — a wick catches for patience, not horsepower. I've tested both, and I have the eyebrows to prove it. Dark arrives whether we're ready or not. The crater provides. I provide the crater. You, tonight, provide the legs.

accept.text: Ooh, lamplighter shift! Rules: west arc first because the wind reads left to right; the proud lamp gets a compliment — any compliment — and the last lamp by the horn hums back. It's allowed. It's been allowed since before allowance.
Station. If the horn's lamp hums when it lights, answer once, politely, and take no requests. Some frequencies are doors, and not every door should be opened by a courier on a schedule.

complete.text: Ninety-one lit, eleven sulks resolved, one proud and *unctuous* about it. I counted twice — counting twice is how I pray. Ring lit before full dark: first time this season. In the ledger that goes down as a stock discrepancy. Minus one dusk.
The horn's lamp spoke tonight, station. Two words. I will not tell you the words. I will tell you they were *thank* and *you*, and that I have filed the incident under weather.

Take the wick ledger's back pages for your codex — centuries of lamps and the hands that kept them. Some entries end mid-sentence and resume a hundred years on, in new ink, mid-thought. Lamp Rest is like that, courier. We don't finish things. We keep them.
